claims.statement: The study tests whether satisfiability bits can induce precise discrete-search behavior without assignment supervision.
Shared recurrent literal/clause messages preserve structural symmetries and produce a satisfiability logit.
Nearly identical paired formulas are generated and labelled using repeated MiniSAT calls.
Clustering embeddings and checking both orientations extracts SAT witnesses; classifier failure is not UNSAT proof.
Classification85%, SATclassification73%, and SATwitness70% are distinct outcomes.
Same checkpoint solves85%of4888SAT-selected graph-decision encodings from roughly10-node graphs using512rounds.
Separate NeuroUNSAT model recognizes three small core templates; no generic UNSAT proof learned.
One fixed random-SAT model reuses SAT reductions for four bounded decision tasks rather than evaluating their cardinality optima.
